items.elicits: Constructs a two-paragraph argument that takes a position addressing both documents, cites evidence from each, explicitly weighs that evidence by each author's point of view, and connects one outside development from the period.

claims.supports: Under these conditions (proctored, individual, AI prohibited and enforced, only the two documents and paper permitted), a compliant response to item 5 licenses the conclusion that this student can construct an argument addressing both documents, use evidence from each, explicitly weigh that evidence by point of view, and connect an accurate outside development -- the whole of H4.
does_not_support: Whether the student can source the documents (author, year, audience) or read them for causal explanation and attitude independently -- H1-H3 are, by the teacher's own account, assessed on the unit test the week before, and Part A here is explicit, ungraded warm-up.

Whether the student's outside-development knowledge is broad -- the rubric credits any one accurate connection, so this shows the student has at least one usable example, not comprehensive command of the period.
Whether the student could produce this argument without the two documents already excerpted and placed in front of them -- locating and vetting primary sources is not part of what this item asks.
Whether this kind of weighing-and-connecting argument holds up on a different document pair or a question not structured as two paired viewpoints -- this is one instance with one pair.

delegation.reason: AI is prohibited and enforced, and the response is produced in class under supervision with only the two documents and paper, so the argument must be the student's own live construction.
